Trap Lore Ross on Q50 Killed Last Night in Chicago (Part 1)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
--------
Trap Lore Ross joins VladTV to react to the tragic death of Chicago rapper Bloodhound Q50, who was killed at just 22 years old after being shot inside a Tesla outside a Chicago gas station.
Ross reflects on Q50's rise alongside Bloodhound Lil Jeff, describing him as an extremely talented young artist whose music was increasingly gaining attention. Vlad recalls interviewing Q50 and being impressed by how professionally he handled difficult questions despite his young age and street background.
The conversation also examines the dangerous lifestyle surrounding Q50's career. Ross discusses Q50's lyrics claiming multiple killings, his alleged involvement in Chicago street conflicts, disrespect toward rivals, and previous incidents outside the city. He also recounts reports that Q50 had been targeted in St. Louis following a financial dispute, raising concerns that numerous unresolved conflicts surrounded the young rapper.
Vlad explains that he previously encouraged Q50 to leave Chicago permanently, noting that even people who believe they "know how to move" can become vulnerable when longstanding street conflicts and revenge are involved. Ross agrees that Q50's growing success couldn't necessarily protect him from enemies connected to his past.
Both reflect on the tragedy of seeing another promising Chicago rapper die so young, following the death of Lil Jeff. Vlad emphasizes that growing older is a privilege many young people take for granted and argues that street decisions made in someone's teens and early twenties can prevent them from ever experiencing the later stages of life.
The conversation concludes with Vlad and Trap Lore Ross paying tribute to Q50 while hoping his death serves as a warning to other young artists caught between growing music careers and ongoing street conflicts.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/4D3wB1ZOXlA
--------
Retired Army Ranger sniper Nicholas Irving joins Shawn Prez to break down why a potential U.S. ground invasion of Iran would be vastly different from past conflicts. Responding to comments from former Navy SEAL Robert O’Neill, Irving compares an Iran war to a far more intense version of Afghanistan, citing Iran’s terrain, larger population, military capabilities, and hardened national mindset.

Drawing on his own combat experience in Afghanistan, Irving explains why mountain warfare, local resistance, and “forever war” dynamics make holding territory nearly impossible without years of prolonged U.S. military presence. He also reflects on the Afghanistan withdrawal, attacks on American forces, and reports involving missiles near military bases in Jordan.

In this candid conversation, Irving argues that while the United States may have power on paper, “winning” a ground war in Iran would be difficult to define—and potentially devastating for troops and civilians alike.

Interview by: Shawn Prez

recentItems.title: Bradford Cohen on Representing YNW Melly for Murder, Why He Left the Case After 6 Months (Part 7)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 6: https://youtu.be/bnLkFwKzsJM
Part 1: https://youtu.be/K7__iCx2ghE
--------
Criminal defense attorney Bradford Cohen joins VladTV to discuss his early role in the YNW Melly murder case, including helping the Florida rapper self-surrender in 2019 after authorities allegedly detained the wrong person at a Pennsylvania show. Cohen explains why he stayed on the case for only five to six months, saying he favored pushing for a speedy trial because he believed the state was not fully prepared and key issues needed to be challenged early. He also weighs in on Melly’s long pretrial detention, Florida bond rules, the mistrial that followed a not-guilty holdout juror, and whether Melly should be considered a flight risk after voluntarily turning himself in. The conversation also touches on the upcoming retrial, possible plea discussions, a co-defendant’s reported 10-year deal, and the stakes of a potential double life sentence.

recentItems.title: Bloodhound Q50, Who Was Killed Today, Tells His Life Story (RIP)
recentItems.description:
In remembrance of Bloodhound Q50, we revisit his conversation with VladTV, where he reflected on his upbringing in Chicago and Gary, Indiana, his family relationships, and the experiences that shaped his life and music.

Q50 spoke about his bond with Bloodhound Lil Jeff, their collaborations, and how Jeff’s passing inspired him to take his rap career more seriously. He also opened up about challenges during his school years, surviving gun violence, and the loss of loved ones. Looking toward his future in music, he discussed his mixtape featuring five songs with Lil Jeff, his relationship with Lil Tjay, and his hopes of collaborating with Polo G and NBA YoungBoy.

Our condolences go out to Q50’s family, friends, and everyone mourning his loss.

--------

In this VladTV interview, Chingy reflects on reconnecting with Nelly after years of tension and finally sharing the stage on Nelly’s 2025 “Where the Party At” tour. The St. Louis rapper says the past issues are “dead,” noting they’ve talked things out and even texted recently as viral clips about their old feud resurface. He also discusses touring with artists including Eve, Ne-Yo, St. Lunatics, Fabolous and Jacquees, and why unity among artists from the same city matters.

Chingy opens up about rivalry in hip-hop, comparisons with Ludacris, media narratives, and how fan division can affect careers. He also addresses Charlamagne Tha God, Wendy Williams, The Breakfast Club, DJ Akademiks, Adam22, YouTube podcasts, Spotify, Patreon, and the responsibility media platforms have when covering artists, including references to Charlamagne’s past legal controversy.

recentItems.description:

Part 5: https://youtu.be/J9ML2ERwweI
Part 1: https://youtu.be/FoBBj-6j544
--------

In this VladTV interview, Max B revisits the murder case that changed his life, addressing the robbery allegations involving Pooh Sims and Gina, the cooperation statement, and the charges he faced, including felony murder, armed robbery, kidnapping, conspiracy, and weapons offenses. The Harlem rapper explains why he accepted a plea deal while facing a potential 75-year sentence and reflects on being arrested after traveling for shows in St. Louis and New Orleans following Hurricane Katrina.

Max B also clears up a long-debated piece of Dipset history: his claim that Jim Jones paid him $120,000 for his publishing, money he says was used toward a $2 million bond. He breaks down the cash paid to the bondsman, the property equity needed for bail, and credits his late partner for putting up buildings to help secure his release. A candid look at music, street life, legal pressure, and survival.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/-pWadYhoSkc
--------
Mario Sanchez sits down with VladTV to discuss the reported Oakland arrests of nine alleged Sureños and why investigators linked the group to 31 Bay Area homicides. Sanchez explains the idea of “upstate Sureños” operating in Northern California, including pockets in Oakland, San Francisco, and Sacramento, and how street politics can differ outside Southern California.

The conversation also turns to Lefty Gunplay, his South Side background, comments about performing in the Bay Area, and a DJ Self interview where the topic came up. Sanchez shares why he believes public online tensions and regional rivalries could make Bay Area shows difficult, even for a professional rapper connected to Kendrick Lamar’s music world. Vlad and Sanchez also debate whether police security changes the risks, and how active street affiliations affect those decisions.
